content:
Facts: The deceased’s brother (later succeeded by his heirs) sought annulment of a public will executed during hospitalization for a brain tumor, alleging the testator’s natural incapacity and undue influence by beneficiaries connected to the support administration; preventive seizure of estate assets had been granted.
Legal framework: Articles 591, 428, 409, and 411 Italian Civil Code; rules on annulment of wills for natural incapacity; legal regime of support administration; principles on burden of proof and assessment of testamentary capacity; relevant Supreme Court case law.
Interpretative issues: (i) The legal standard for “natural incapacity” sufficient to annul a will and its temporal assessment at the moment of execution; (ii) the evidentiary weight of medical records, guardianship measures, and subsequent acts in proving incapacity; (iii) whether the opening of support administration limits testamentary capacity absent an express judicial restriction; (iv) proof of psychological coercion or undue influence on the testator’s free determination.
Principles applied: A will by an adult not legally incapacitated is valid unless the challenger proves that, at the precise time of execution, the testator was wholly incapable of understanding and self-determination; sporadic confusion, serious illness, or hospitalization do not suffice absent continuity and intensity affecting volition; support administration does not per se limit the capacity to make a will, which remains intact unless expressly restricted by the guardianship judge under Article 411 Civil Code; the burden of proof of natural incapacity and undue influence lies with the claimant and requires clear, consistent presumptions; contemporaneous acts evidencing lucidity, coherent testamentary content, medical assessments attesting capacity, and the absence of concrete proof of coercion confirm the validity of the will and justify revocation of preventive seizure. ID: ITI117; Instance_Type: First instance; Legal_Duration: P4Y; Law: IT – Civil Code – 591(3)
